app.tagline: Windows trainers in your Proton prefixes
app.ready: ArchMod ready. Select a game to begin.
app.configResetBackup: Configuration reset. Previous file kept at: {path}
app.copyFailed: Copy failed: the clipboard is unavailable.
main.emptyTitle: Pick a game from the list
main.emptyText: ArchMod links a Windows trainer to each Steam game and injects it into its Proton prefix, without touching a terminal.
main.noPrefixHint: The prefix is created the first time the game runs through Steam
main.tabLauncherHint: Run a Windows trainer inside the Proton prefix
main.tabPanelHint: Turn on options from a community profile
main.tabWorkshopHint: Build a profile: probe an address and save it
main.noTrainerLinked: No trainer is linked to this game yet.
main.trainerMissingWarning: The file no longer exists at this location. Import the trainer again to restore the link.
main.notRunningWarning: The game is not detected: start it from Steam before injecting the trainer (you will be asked to confirm).
console.title: Console
console.empty: Output from protontricks, Proton and Wine appears here as it happens.
dialog.notRunningTitle: The game does not seem to be running
settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Missing translations fall back to English.
settings.backendAutoHint: protontricks if present, then native Proton, then system Wine.
settings.backendProtontricksHint: The reference command, run inside the game prefix.
settings.backendProtonHint: The game's own proton script, no extra dependency.
settings.backendWineHint: WINEPREFIX pointed at compatdata. May alter the prefix.
settings.warnLabel: Warn when the game is not running
settings.warnHint: Ask for confirmation before injecting a trainer into a closed game.
settings.artworkHint: Use the Steam CDN when the local cache has no image.
panel.gameNotRunningHint: Memory addresses only exist while the game runs. Start it from Steam — or pick another game, the « Running » filter shows only those.
panel.noProfileHint: A profile lists a game's options and where their values live in memory. Get one from the community repository, or build your own in the Workshop tab.
panel.outdated: Written for build {profile}, you are on {installed} — some addresses may have moved.
workshop.name: Option name
workshop.needsRunning: Start the game to probe an address.
workshop.buildNote: Build {build} — a profile is only valid for the game version it was recorded on.
workshop.emptyProfile: No options yet. Probe an address, then add it.
workshop.duplicateId: An option already uses the identifier « {id} ».
prefix.title: Proton prefix
prefix.installStarted: Installation started — follow the progress in the console.
prefix.note: Installing a component goes through protontricks and takes several minutes: progress appears in the console.
scanner.tabHint: Find a value in memory and freeze it
scanner.how: Search for a number you can read in game, change it in game, then search again: the intersection isolates the address.
scanner.anchoredHint: Inside a module: this address can become a lasting profile
scanner.volatileHint: Heap memory: this address changes on every launch
scanner.narrow: Showing {shown} of {total} — narrow further to see them all.
scanner.noResult: No match. Check the value type, or try another filter.
scanner.needsValue: Enter a number for this filter.
scanner.pointerNote: An address found in the heap only holds for this session. Turning it into a shareable profile would need a pointer scan, which is not implemented yet.
pointer.hunting: Following pointers back from {address} — this scans the whole memory, allow a few seconds.
pointer.title: Pointer paths to {address}
pointer.none: No static path found. Try again from another candidate, or the value may only be reachable through a longer chain.
pointer.adopted: Path added to the workshop profile.
pointer.mismatch: This path no longer leads to the same address — discard it.
pointer.verifyNote: Shorter paths are more robust: they cross fewer structures that a game update could change. Each path is replayed and verified before being added.
script.title: Auto-assembler script
script.explain: This script creates the symbols the table's entries depend on: it finds the pattern, writes a small block of code into the game and diverts an instruction towards it. Only a narrow subset of the Cheat Engine language is supported — anything else is refused rather than guessed.
script.warning: Modifies the running game. Save first.
script.done: Script run: {count} symbols published, code at {address}.
